name: Shopify
summary: Shopify supports OAuth2 (authorization code grant for public apps and client‑credentials grant for internal apps). First create a Partner app in the Dev Dashboard, configure redirect URIs and scopes, then use the standard OAuth flow.

oauth_note.text: Public apps use the OAuth2 authorization code grant; internal apps can use the client‑credentials grant (no redirect).

app_types.name: Public (installed) app
app_types.when_to_use: App that merchants install on their stores

app_types.name: Custom/internal app
app_types.when_to_use: App that only accesses stores in your own organization

registration_access_claim.text: Only users with a Shopify Partner account can create apps in the Dev Dashboard.

prerequisites.text: Shopify Partner account and access to the Dev Dashboard
App client ID and client secret from the Dev Dashboard
One or more redirect URIs added to the app settings

steps.title: Create a new app in the Partner Dev Dashboard
steps.detail: Log into partners.shopify.com, click ‘Apps’, then ‘Create app’. Choose Public or Custom as needed.

steps.title: Record the client ID and client secret
steps.detail: In the app’s Settings page copy the ‘API key’ (client ID) and ‘API secret key’ (client secret).

steps.title: Add redirect URI(s) to the app
steps.detail: In Settings → App setup, add the exact URL(s) your app will receive the OAuth callback on. They must match the URI you’ll use later.

steps.title: Build the authorization URL
steps.detail: Construct https://{shop}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/authorize?client_id={client_id}&scope={comma‑separated‑scopes}&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}&state={nonce}&grant_options[]=offline (optional). Include a random state value.

steps.title: Redirect the merchant to the URL
steps.detail: Send the merchant’s browser to the URL; Shopify shows the permission screen.

steps.title: Validate the callback
steps.detail: When Shopify redirects back, verify the state matches, compute HMAC‑SHA256 of the query string using the client secret and compare to the hmac parameter, and ensure the shop domain matches ^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9\-]*\.myshopify\.com$

steps.title: Exchange the code for an access token
steps.detail: POST to the token endpoint (as listed in the OpenID discovery document) with client_id, client_secret, code and redirect_uri. Receive an offline access token (24‑hour expiry) or online token as requested.

steps.title: Store the token and use it in API calls
steps.detail: Include the token in the X‑Shopify‑Access‑Token header on GraphQL Admin API requests.

approval_claim.text: Certain sensitive scopes require Shopify’s approval before a public app can request them.

unreviewed_limits.text: Apps using only non‑restricted scopes can be installed on development stores without any additional review.

review_artifacts.text: Justification for restricted scopes (e.g., protected customer data)
Privacy policy URL (required for public apps)

approval_wait.note: Docs do not specify a review timeline.

setup_time.note: Hands‑on time to create the app and obtain credentials.

redirect_uri_rules.text: The redirect URI must exactly match one of the URIs configured in the Dev Dashboard; no wildcards. HTTPS is recommended but not explicitly required in the docs.

token_lifecycle.text: Authorization code flow returns an offline access token that persists across sessions; tokens expire after 24 hours (client‑credentials grant also 24 h). No refresh token; request a new token when expired.

scopes_note.text: Scopes are a comma‑separated list; some scopes (e.g., protected customer data) trigger additional requirements and may need Shopify approval.

instance_specific.text: API calls are made against a specific shop’s domain {shop}.myshopify.com; tokens are scoped to that shop.

pkce_required.text: PKCE support is mentioned in the discovery document but not required by the official docs; not mentioned in the provided sources.

blockers.blocker: Redirect URI does not exactly match the one configured
blockers.fix: Add the exact URI in the app settings or update the URL used in the auth request.
Store the generated state nonce, compare it on callback, and compute HMAC‑SHA256 using the client secret as described.

blockers.blocker: Requesting a restricted scope without Shopify approval
blockers.fix: Submit a scope justification via the Partner Dashboard or remove the scope until approved.

blockers.blocker: Using client‑credentials grant on a shop that isn’t in your organization (shop_not_permitted error)
blockers.fix: Only use client‑credentials for stores you own; for external merchants use the authorization code flow.

agent_can: parse the OpenID discovery document for endpoints
exchange authorization code for token (POST request)
call GraphQL Admin API with X‑Shopify‑Access‑Token header
human_must: create the app in the Dev Dashboard
configure redirect URIs and select scopes
review and accept any required scope approvals
composio_note: Composio has a 'shopify' toolkit (https://docs.composio.dev/kb/toolkit/shopify). Composio's own OAuth credential guide for it: https://composio.dev/auth/shopify. When registering, use the redirect URI shown in your Composio auth config.
